text: A straight-line falling across  parallel straight-lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another,  the external (angle) equal to the internal and opposite (angle), and the (sum of the) internal (angles) on the same side equal to two right-angles.   For let the straight-line $EF$ fall across the parallel straight-lines $AB$ and $CD$. I say that it makes the  alternate angles, $AGH$ and $GHD$,  equal,  the external angle $EGB$ equal to the internal and opposite (angle) $GHD$, and the (sum of the) internal (angles) on the same side, $BGH$ and $GHD$, equal to two right-angles.
For if $AGH$ is unequal to $GHD$ then one of them is greater.
assertion: if AGH is unequal to GHD then one of them is greater

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: For if $AGH$ is unequal to $GHD$ then one of them is greater.

text: Let $BGH$ have been added to both.
assertion: BGH has been added to both sides

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: Let $BGH$ have been added to both.

text: Thus, (the sum of) $AGH$ and $BGH$ is greater than (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AGH$ and $BGH$ is greater than (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$

text: But, (the sum of) $AGH$ and $BGH$ is equal to two right-angles [Prop~1.13].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AGH$ and $BGH$ is equal to two right-angles

text: Thus,  (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$ is [also] less than two right-angles.
assertion: BGH + GHD is less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $BGH$ and $GHD$ is [also] less than two right-angles

text: But (straight-lines) being produced to infinity from (internal angles whose sum is) less than two right-angles meet together [Post.~5].
assertion: straight-lines from angles summing to less than two right-angles will meet when produced to infinity

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: But (straight-lines) being produced to infinity from (internal angles whose sum is) less than two right-angles meet together

text: Thus, $AB$ and $CD$, being produced to infinity, will meet together.
assertion: AB and CD will meet when produced to infinity

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AB$ and $CD$, being produced to infinity, will meet together

text: But they do not meet, on account of them (initially) being assumed parallel (to one another) [Def.~1.23].
assertion: AB and CD do not meet (contradiction with parallel assumption)

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: them (initially) being assumed parallel (to one another)

assertion: AGH is not unequal to GHD

text: And $EGB$ is thus also equal to $GHD$.

assertion: BGH added to both EGB and GHD

text: Thus, (the sum of) $EGB$ and $BGH$ is equal to (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $EGB$ and $BGH$ is equal to (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$

text: But, (the sum of) $EGB$ and $BGH$ is equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.13].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $EGB$ and $BGH$ is equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, (the sum of) $BGH$ and $GHD$ is also equal to two right-angles.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $BGH$ and $GHD$ is also equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, a straight-line falling across parallel straight-lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another,  the external (angle) equal to the internal and opposite (angle), and the (sum of the) internal (angles) on the same side equal to two right-angles. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
